The 30-minute lesson on O3 is written, and a quiz is ready when you are. I didn't open the lesson in a browser or run a word count, so its length and layout are unchecked. I estimate it at about 3,800 words, inside the 30-minute range.

**Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`

It covers, using your laser-cutter question as the running example:
- **The context window:** what the model can see in one call, and what tokens are.
- **What is kept between steps:** the model remembers nothing, so your program re-sends the whole message list on every call.
- **Cost and accuracy:** a worked token count (10,010 tokens read over four calls), plus why a fuller context also makes key facts harder for the model to find.
- **Between sessions:** saving short notes outside the model, such as a student's training status, and loading them next time.
- **Retrieval:** a search tool that pulls a few chunks of the long manuals into the context.

It includes three figures, practice checks with instant feedback, and a closing exercise where you sort the assistant's information into context, notes or searched manuals. The token budget in the worked example uses made-up round numbers, and the lesson says so.

**Also written:**
- **Quiz:** `quizzes/0002.json`, with five items. Its key is in `keys/0002.json`, so I haven't shown any answers here.
- **Cheat sheet:** `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html`, a one-page version of the lesson to look things up.
- **Sources:** `RESOURCES.md`, with the three sources I used. The main one is Anthropic's [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents).
- **Notes:** `NOTES.md` is updated with where this lesson leaves you.

Retrieval methods (how to chunk the manuals, keyword versus meaning-based search) are only touched on here and could be the next lesson. Quiz 0001 is still ungraded, and I can grade it whenever you like.

Ask me anything about the lesson in the chat.
